cases.purpose: Ctrl-C cleanup with observed signal prerequisites and foreground group using mouse builtin.
cases.script:
saved=$(/bin/stty -g) || exit 21
/bin/stty -icanon -echo isig intr ^C min 1 time 0 || exit 22
trap '/bin/stty "$saved"' EXIT
trap 'mouse disable all; /bin/stty "$saved"; printf "\nINT-CLEANED\n"; exit 130' INT
mouse enable all
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os,signal; p=os.getppid(); assert os.tcgetpgrp(0)==os.getpgrp()==p; d=dict(line.split(":",1) for line in open("/proc/%d/status"%p) if ":" in line); assert all(not (int(d[k],16) & (1 << (signal.SIGINT-1))) for k in ("SigIgn","SigBlk"))' || exit 26
printf 'READY-INT\n'
IFS= read -r -N 1 unused
exit 25
cases.oracle: XTerm mouse tracking protocol (SGR 1006, urxvt 1015, legacy X10) and documented mouse record format. Injected input is independently hand-encoded; the consumer is fixture Bash code. This is a byte-stream lifecycle, not a terminal-emulator mode-state assertion.
cases.comparison: Observe ISIG, VINTR and an unblocked foreground SIGINT before injecting Ctrl-C; require the same cleanup bytes, marker, status and restored termios as the historical case.
